Build a set of candidate detection functions

Source: R/model-set.R
model_set.Rd

Expands key functions, adjustment series and covariate formulas into a grid of candidate models, one row per candidate. Pass the result to sweep_models() to fit them all.

Usage

model_set(key = c("hn", "hr"), adjustment = NULL, order = NULL, formula = ~1)

Arguments

key

Character vector of key functions: any of "hn", "hr", "unif", "gamma". Default c("hn", "hr").

adjustment

Character vector of adjustment series: "cos" (cosine), "herm" (Hermite polynomial) or "poly" (simple polynomial). One candidate per series. NULL (default) fits no adjustment terms.

order

Integer vector of highest adjustment orders, one candidate per element. Orders are cumulative, as in Distance::ds(): a candidate carries every term of its series up to order. For example, order = 3 on "hn" with "cos" fits adj.order = c(2, 3). Cosine orders run 2, 3, 4, ... (1, 2, 3, ... for "unif"). Hermite and polynomial orders run 4, 6, 8, ... (2, 4, 6, ... for "unif"). NULL (default) gives the first term of the series only. An order outside its series is dropped with a warning. Ignored when adjustment is NULL.

formula

One-sided formula, or a list of them, giving detection covariates. ~1 (default) means no covariates and fits with cds; any other formula fits with mcds.

Value

A tibble with one row per candidate and columns:

model_id

Label, e.g. "hn", "hr+cos(2,3)", "hn wt_beaufort".

key

Key function.

adjustment

Adjustment series, or NA.

order

Highest adjustment order, or NA.

formula

Covariate formula as a string.

dsmodel

The model formula string passed to mrds::ddf().

How it works

  1. Checks that every key, adjustment series, order and formula is valid.

  2. Crosses keys, series, orders and formulas into a grid.

  3. Drops, with a warning, candidates that cannot be fitted meaningfully: a uniform key with no adjustment, a uniform key with covariates, and an adjustment order outside its series.

  4. Builds each candidate's mrds model string and its model_id label.

  5. Drops, with a warning, duplicate candidates.

Key functions

"hn"

Half-normal. A shoulder at zero and a smooth fall-off. The usual default.

"hr"

Hazard-rate. A broader shoulder and a heavier tail, with a second parameter.

"unif"

Uniform. Detection is certain out to the truncation distance, which is a strip transect. It is kept only with adjustment terms. It takes no covariates, because it has no scale parameter for them to act on.

"gamma"

Gamma. Unimodal, with its peak away from zero, so detection is lowest on the track-line. mrds scales it to 1 at its peak, not at zero. Not available in Distance::ds().

Gamma key and left truncation

An aircraft cannot see the water directly beneath it, and a ship cannot see past its bow wave. For such a platform the gamma key fits the near distances better than a half-normal, which must peak at zero. Left truncation models the same blind spot by discarding the near distances. Use one or the other, not both. sweep_models() takes left and warns if it is set for a model set that contains the gamma key.

References

Buckland, S.T., Anderson, D.R., Burnham, K.P., Laake, J.L., Borchers, D.L. and Thomas, L. (2001) Introduction to Distance Sampling. Oxford University Press.

Laake, J.L. and Borchers, D.L. (2004) Methods for incomplete detection at distance zero. In Advanced Distance Sampling, Oxford University Press.

Becker, E.A. and Quang, P.X. (2009) A gamma-shaped detection function for line-transect surveys with mark-recapture and covariate data. Journal of Agricultural, Biological and Environmental Statistics 14:207-223. doi:10.1198/jabes.2009.0013 Source of the gamma key, developed for aerial surveys.

See also

sweep_models()

Examples

# Default: half-normal and hazard-rate, no adjustments or covariates
model_set()
#> # A tibble: 2 × 6
#>   model_id key   adjustment order formula dsmodel                           
#>   <chr>    <chr> <chr>      <int> <chr>   <chr>                             
#> 1 hn       hn    NA            NA ~1      "~cds(key = \"hn\", formula = ~1)"
#> 2 hr       hr    NA            NA ~1      "~cds(key = \"hr\", formula = ~1)"

# Cosine adjustments up to orders 2 and 3
model_set(key = c("hn", "hr"), adjustment = "cos", order = 2:3)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 6
#>   model_id    key   adjustment order formula dsmodel                            
#>   <chr>       <chr> <chr>      <int> <chr>   <chr>                              
#> 1 hn+cos(2)   hn    cos            2 ~1      "~cds(key = \"hn\", formula = ~1, …
#> 2 hr+cos(2)   hr    cos            2 ~1      "~cds(key = \"hr\", formula = ~1, …
#> 3 hn+cos(2,3) hn    cos            3 ~1      "~cds(key = \"hn\", formula = ~1, …
#> 4 hr+cos(2,3) hr    cos            3 ~1      "~cds(key = \"hr\", formula = ~1, …

# With and without a detection covariate
model_set(key = "hn", formula = list(~1, ~wt_beaufort))
#> # A tibble: 2 × 6
#>   model_id       key   adjustment order formula      dsmodel                    
#>   <chr>          <chr> <chr>      <int> <chr>        <chr>                      
#> 1 hn             hn    NA            NA ~1           "~cds(key = \"hn\", formul…
#> 2 hn wt_beaufort hn    NA            NA ~wt_beaufort "~mcds(key = \"hn\", formu…

# The gamma key, for a platform that cannot see beneath itself
model_set(key = c("hn", "gamma"))
#> # A tibble: 2 × 6
#>   model_id key   adjustment order formula dsmodel                              
#>   <chr>    <chr> <chr>      <int> <chr>   <chr>                                
#> 1 hn       hn    NA            NA ~1      "~cds(key = \"hn\", formula = ~1)"   
#> 2 gamma    gamma NA            NA ~1      "~cds(key = \"gamma\", formula = ~1)"
